messages:
ashwin: Ran nsys slice on the FP8 serving cluster with a 10k request replay. Seeing periodic host->device memcpy spikes around step 2 of decode, and dequant kernels are tiny but hostcopy is huge. timeline attached (link): https://redwood-internal/trace/1765426789 :eyes:

ashwin: command i used:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace --sample=none --trace=cuda,cublas,cudnn python reproduce.py --batch 8 --seq 1024 --model fp8-small
```

mira: can you paste the top nvprof summary or a cut of the timeline? is it the same on Dedicated nodes?

ashwin: nvprof top snippet:
```
GPU activities:
  dequantize_fp8_kernel    0.12 ms  12 calls
  matmul_qgemm_fp8         0.45 ms   12 calls
  cudaMemcpyHostToDevice   1.86 ms   24 calls
```
host side shows memcpy stalls coalesced with small kernels so latency adds up.

kat: hmm, looks like batching heuristic is producing tiny micro-batches that prevent kernel fusion. FP8 path has a host-side dequant fallback for some ops when kernel not supported. could we be falling back because of odd sequence lengths? :thinking:

samir: do we have a map of kernel selection rules? maybe the runtime picks the FP8 path but the matmul kernel isn't available so we dequant, copy, run fp32 matmul on GPU? that would explain extra memcpy.

ashwin: i traced the decision log: 'kernel_selector: chose fp8_variant; requires dequant_host=true; fallback_matmul=fp32' — attached log lines.

kat: proposal: change batching heuristic to prefer batch sizes that align with fp8 kernel tiling (multiples of 32) for seq_len>512. Also add a runtime check to prefer device-dequant fused kernel when available.

mira: can you try re-run with --batch 32 and pin to node with latest kernels (kernel v1.4.2)?

ashwin: re-run results quick:
```
--batch 8: avg per-token 1.9ms, hostcopy cost ~45%
--batch 32: avg per-token 1.2ms, hostcopy cost ~12%, dequant kernel on-device
```

perfbot: Automated note: created perf ticket PERF-2034 for 'FP8 hostcopy hotspots on small batches' and linked trace.

samir: will put a short CANARY to prefer fused device-dequant kernel when available; also add metric to Console for hostcopy ratio per route.

kat: add an eval to Redwood Optimize to detect accuracy drift when switching from host-dequant to device-dequant (FP8->FP32 cast differences). we should guard with a small eval set.

mira: thanks, this explains the spike. next steps: ashwin to open trace + nvtx, samir to PR batching heuristic, kat to add eval. :thumbsup:
